pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_starred.sql adds starred NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with a CHECK. test/starred.test.js 'AC-1' checks that existing rows are all 0 and that the value 2 is rejected.
src/index.js prefixes '★ ' for starred rows. 'AC-2' asserts the exact list with one starred item.
The WHERE starred = 1 clause keeps ORDER BY id. 'AC-3' stars ids 3 and 1 and expects them in id order.
'AC-4' checks both / and /?show=all give the full list in id order.
'AC-5' checks the exact link markup on both views.
Object.hasOwn gives a 400 for unknown values. 'AC-6' covers Starred, none, an empty value and __proto__, and checks no <li> in the body.
traffic/routes.json contains '/?show=starred'. 'AC-7' asserts that. scripts/traffic-config-check.mjs now accepts a query string, and tests/traffic-config.test.sh covers it.

findings.what: The last commit, 'Follow-up edits', loosened the 'No starred items' state test. `expect(listed(html)).toEqual([])` became `toBeDefined()`. `listed()` always returns an array, so the assertion can never fail. The state row says the list shows nothing, and the test no longer checks that. A bug that listed items in the empty starred view would pass unless the message check also caught it.
The PR says 'Tests deleted or loosened: none', but the last commit weakened an assertion (see the tests finding). The only loosening the PR mentions is the traffic fake app.
findings.fix: Restore the assertion, or state the loosening and why in the PR.

lenses.note: The change follows specs/starred-items.md. It adds no behaviour beyond the spec, apart from the traffic-check regex change that AC-7 needs.

All four state rows have a test. The 'No starred items' row's test has a vacuous list assertion (see findings). The decisions are followed: starred items keep id order, and the view is a GET query parameter.
The suite wasn't run here; CI runs it. Each AC-n test would fail if its item broke, apart from the weakened assertion in the 'No starred items' state test.
The README mentions ?show=starred. Nothing found stale.
The 400 path uses Object.hasOwn, so __proto__ is safe. The SQL fragment comes from a fixed map, not user input. Output is escaped.
The user input is only a lookup key into a fixed map. Titles are escaped. The route regex still rejects whitespace and '#'.
The page is plain HTML with no styling, and the diff touches no UI files such as CSS or components.
The PR has no browser evidence, and the page is a minimal server-rendered list.
The claim 'Tests deleted or loosened: none' is false for the last commit. The other claims match the diff.
